transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-06
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42m
Attendees: Alice Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Jane Soto (Fintra - Head of ML), Tom Barker (Fintra - Platform), Riya Singh (Fintra - InfoSec)

Auto-summary (brief): Quick walkthrough of Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching and caching. Went through cost model examples for 100M tokens/month and a sample prefix hit-rate sensitivity. Customer asked about dedicated capacity and encryption/KMS. Agreed to run pilot and share docs.

Transcript (note: auto-transcription may contain errors):
[00:00] Alice Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we're gonna walk through optimize, specifically batching and caching recommendations. i've put the slides in the chat, link: https://redwood.company/s/optimize-batching (shared).
[00:18] Jane Soto: cool, thanks. quick context - we're planning to replace our old retrieval+lm pipeline for customer support with an in-house assistant. expect median request length is low, but long context on follow-ups, and about 100M tokens / mo projected for phase 1.
[00:30] Marcus Patel: got it. two immediate constraints we heard - latency SLO (95p under ~300ms) and strict data controls; curious how batching/caching nudges cost. i'll show numbers in a sec.
[00:45] Tom Barker: also our platform prefers VPC/private deployment for the pilot, and we're evaluating dedicated capacity because of predictable throughput.
[00:58] Alice Chen: perfect. high level - batching lets you amortize GPU overhead but increases tail latency; caching (prefix and KV) reduces token generation cost when you have repeated prefixes or conversation state. we'll step through practical configs.
[01:20] Marcus Patel: (screen share) okay slide 3: simple cost model. baseline hosted model at 1.2M tokens per dollar (example), with throughput of 120 tokens/sec on a shared 8xA100 equivalent instance. if we enable continuous batching with a batch target of 16 and min latency knobs, throughput improves by ~2.5x but p95 latency worsens by ~20-40ms depending on queue depth. numbers are approximate - these are from our runtime profiling.
[02:05] Riya Singh: when you say "continuous batching," is that at the Redwood side only or something we tune on the client?
[02:12] Marcus Patel: it's on the serving runtime side; you configure target batch sizes and max wait (ms). Redwood Optimize suggests configs per traffic pattern; customers can lock in to a config in Dedicated.
[02:34] Jane Soto: show us cache types - prefix vs KV, what's the difference again?
[02:41] Marcus Patel: sure. prefix cache is a simple LRU of common starting tokens/embeddings - it's great when conversations begin with a template or product name. KV cache is per-session key-value cache that stores transformer KV states so repeated prefixes or long context only re-generate new tokens; this is more storage-heavy but gives much higher hit-rate on multi-turns. prefix cache reduces model compute for repeated opening prompts; KV cache reduces autoregressive token compute when the identical KV states exist.
[03:15] Luis Ortega: a practical example: for support flows, if a 30% of sessions repeat the exact product intro, prefix hits cut token costs by ~25% in our benchmarks. with KV caching for follow-ups where the first 50 tokens are identical, you can reduce token generation cost on avg ~40-60% for those sessions.
[03:45] Tom Barker: how do you handle cache invalidation? sensitive data could get reused incorrectly.
[03:52] Marcus Patel: important Q. Redwood's caching has rules: you can opt-in per route, and set TTLs and session-scoped caches. Sensitive or PII-containing prompts can be marked not-cacheable at the SDK layer; for Dedicated/Private we can also disable persistent cache or encrypt cache with customer-managed KMS. Riya?
[04:18] Riya Singh: ok, encryption at rest for cache and auditability are must-haves. also we need to prove data residency for EU users.
[04:26] Alice Chen: noted. we have Private with VPC and on-prem options; for pilot we can run Dedicated in a region that meets residency and plug in your KMS. we'll share SOC2 docs.
[04:40] Marcus Patel: back to cost math - slide 6: sensitivity table for 100M tokens/mo. baseline (no caching, small batch) - $X (placeholder) = assume $1200/mo. Add batching improvements -> 30% lower cost per token, KV cache with 30% hit-rate -> additional 25% savings; combined could net ~45-55% cost reduction depending on hit-rate and model size. those percents are from internal profiling; exact numbers depend on model, sequence length and hit-rate.
[05:30] Jane Soto: those sound promising; can you share the raw spreadsheet?
[05:35] Marcus Patel: yes, i'll share a benchmark workbook. it models per-token compute, disk cost for KV cache, and amortized GPU hours for dedicated pools. link will be in follow-up.
[05:48] Tom Barker: curious about memory join - for KV cache you said storage heavy; what's the operational overhead on Dedicated?
[05:55] Luis Ortega: depends on sessions retained. for example if you keep 10k active sessions and avg KV tape per session is 200KB, that's ~2GB memory plus indexing, plus extra IO. we usually suggest an LRU eviction at 24-48 hrs for typical support use. dedicated boxes can be provisioned with nvram/ram for caching; Optimize will recommend based on traffic profile.
[06:30] Jane Soto: can caching skew responses? like stale context?
[06:36] Marcus Patel: can if you don't flush correctly. that's why we recommend session-scoped KV with clear TTLs and SDK signals for user identity changes. we also support explicit cache flush via API.
[06:50] Riya Singh: how do you prove caching didn't exfiltrate PII across sessions?
[06:55] Marcus Patel: audit logs tie cached hits to session IDs and request hashes; in Dedicated/Private those logs are shipped to your SIEM and can be retained per your retention policy. we can also disable cross-session caches entirely.
[07:20] Alice Chen: let's show a sample config for your expected traffic. Marcus?
[07:25] Marcus Patel: (screen) sample traffic: 20 req/s peak, median payload 60 tokens, follow-ups average 4 turns. recommended config: batch target 12, max wait 25ms, kv-cache enabled with per-session TTL 36h, prefix cache for route '/support/faq' with TTL 7d. Estimated impact: 95p latency goes from 280ms to 310ms with batching on hosted; with Dedicated and tuned batch timeouts we can keep 95p ~290ms while still getting ~40% cost reductions. note these are estimations.
[08:20] Tom Barker: 310ms is above our 300ms SLO - can you tune to keep under 300?
[08:26] Marcus Patel: yes, tuning knobs: reduce batch target to 8 or lower max wait. you lose some batching efficiency but regain latency headroom. for Dedicated we can do prioritized lanes so latency-sensitive routes skip batching and go to a low-queue pool.
[08:45] Jane Soto: prioritized lanes sounds useful - is that a config flag?
[08:49] Luis Ortega: yes, it's a per-route policy. you can pin routes to low-latency pool or cost-optimized pool, routing enforced by the platform.
[09:05] Riya Singh: what's the fallback if Dedicated capacity is saturated? we can't have downtime for payments-related flows.
[09:12] Alice Chen: Redwood supports smart routing and automatic fallback to hosted compatible model variants. you can set policies: prefer dedicated, fallback to hosted with a smaller model, or queue requests. for payments flows you'd typically set no fallback and route to a higher priority dedicated pool.
[09:34] Jane Soto: model selection - are you forcing a specific family? we need to ensure response quality.
[09:40] Marcus Patel: we provide a model catalog with performance profiles; Optimize will recommend quantization and model size tradeoffs. you can pin versions and run A/B or canary rollouts. quality regression alerts tie to prompt evals.
[09:58] Tom Barker: for the cost model - how do you account for storage / egress / KMS calls?
[10:04] Marcus Patel: cost model includes incremental storage for KV caches, periodic snapshotting, and KMS per-decrypt cost. we show both pure compute token cost and incremental infra costs. I'll include a line in the sheet for KMS ops: e.g., 1M decrypts / mo ~ $Y - depends on your KMS provider.
[10:30] Jane Soto: any weird edge cases? like long context windows causing batch fragmentation?
[10:35] Luis Ortega: longer context increases per-request compute and can reduce batching efficiency because sequence lengths are variable; Optimize looks at sequence length distribution to pick batch targets and kernel selection. for very long sequences, we sometimes recommend different model variants / offloading strategies.
[10:55] Riya Singh: security notes - we need SAML SSO for the console, RBAC per-team, and audit log retention 7 years for compliance.
[11:04] Alice Chen: we support SSO/SAML, RBAC, and configurable log retention for Private and Dedicated. we'll send the SOC2 and a sample audit-schema.
[11:18] Jane Soto: are there any benchmarks you can share for kv hit-rate sensitivity? like a table showing cost vs hit-rate?
[11:24] Marcus Patel: yes (shows slide): at 0% KV hit-rate baseline cost C. at 10% hit-rate ~8% savings, 30% hit-rate ~25% savings, 50% hit-rate ~40% savings. combined with batching (30% lower per-token compute) you get multiplicative benefits.
[12:00] Tom Barker: can the KV cache be sharded across nodes? we can't have single point of failure for cache storage.
[12:06] Luis Ortega: yes, we shard and replicate; for Dedicated we recommend local memory-first caches with persistent backing; in Private deployments you can choose on-prem storage.
[12:22] Jane Soto: what's the typical pilot cadence? we want to see production-like traffic with instrumentation.
[12:28] Alice Chen: typical pilot is 2 weeks of perf tests: you give sample traffic, we provision a small dedicated pool or private instance, run benchmark, and iterate config. deliverables include benchmark workbook, recommended config, and pilot summary.
[12:45] Riya Singh: for the pilot, we need to ensure encryption keys are customer-managed. can that be arranged?
[12:50] Marcus Patel: yes, in Dedicated/Private you can bring-your-own KMS/HSM; we'll instrument the endpoints to call your KMS for key material.
[13:05] Jane Soto: ok looks good. any limitations for multi-tenant environments? we are multi-tenant internally across product lines.
[13:12] Luis Ortega: routing policies let you isolate tenant workloads; for strict isolation we'd recommend Dedicated per tenant or use RBAC/route-level quotas in Private.
[13:28] Tom Barker: one more - we use an internal embedding index plus retrieval. does caching play nicely with retrieval-augmented flows?
[13:35] Marcus Patel: yes, typical pattern: retrieval supplies context; prefix cache helps if retrieval returns same doc snippets frequently; KV cache helps if the returned context and prior tokens match exactly across turns. we recommend an endpoint per-route to tune caching.
[13:55] Jane Soto: any pitfalls on evaluation metrics? what should we measure?
[13:59] Marcus Patel: measure token cost, p95 latency, KV hit-rate, batch occupancy, and failure rate. Optimize dashboard exposes these metrics per model/route.
[14:20] Alice Chen: let's do a quick live example. Marcus, run the demo payload with kv on/off?
[14:25] Marcus Patel: sure. (pauses) running sample - first request, no cache hit, tokens generated 78, latency 190ms. second request with identical prefix - KV hit, tokens generated 12, latency 80ms. transcript: the stream may show slight stutter - sorry for noise, network is flaky.
[15:05] Tom Barker: nice. can we see the audit log entry?
[15:09] Marcus Patel: showing log: request_id, session_id, cache_hit:true, kv_key: hashed, model: rwd-2b, latency_ms: 82. note hashed keys to avoid exposing PII in logs.
[15:28] Riya Singh: hashed keys ok, we still need to ensure hash is salted tenant-wise to avoid cross-tenant correlation.
[15:35] Marcus Patel: agree. we support tenant salts in hashing and per-tenant encryption keys.
[15:42] Jane Soto: ok, high level - what's the lift to run a pilot?
[15:48] Alice Chen: minimal; we need sample traffic (Tom), SOC/KMS access for test (Riya), and an AE+SE kickoff. We'll provision a dedicated small pool for two weeks.
[16:00] Tom Barker: timeline - can we start next week?
[16:03] Alice Chen: yes, target pilot kickoff week of 2026-03-15.
[16:08] Jane Soto: one last question: how do rollouts affect cache coherency when you deploy a new model version?
[16:14] Luis Ortega: when you change model versions we automatically invalidate caches tied to model fingerprint unless you opt to keep them; common practice is to invalidate on major version bumps to avoid stale representation differences.
[16:28] Riya Singh: please include that in the runbook.
[16:32] Marcus Patel: will do.
[16:36] Alice Chen: ok recap and next steps - i'll send pricing/pilot SOW and SOC2 pack; Marcus will send benchmark spreadsheet and sample configs; Tom will share traffic profile; Riya will confirm KMS/SAML specifics.
[16:52] Jane Soto: thanks all.
[16:55] Alice Chen: thanks, we'll follow up by end of week.

End.
